meta.title: Adylsha Yumayev | Software Engineer — C#/.NET & Backend
meta.description: Adylsha Yumayev — Software Engineer focused on C#/.NET, ASP.NET Core, SQL Server, and backend engineering. hero.description: I build backend systems and APIs with C#, ASP.NET Core, and SQL Server — from enterprise applications to independently built systems in identity management and real-time infrastructure. I'm currently deepening my focus on system design and software architecture.

about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: Backend engineer, moving toward software architecture
about.p1: Over four years, I've worked mainly on backend systems for enterprise software — API development, database structures on SQL Server, and internal platforms supporting real business workflows. I also contributed to the architecture of my current company's first mobile application.
about.p2: Outside of work, I build backend-heavy systems that let me explore identity, distributed systems, observability, and system design in depth. My projects include YumaIdentity, an identity and access management service, YumaSnap, a real-time event platform, and YumaLog, a logging and observability library.
about.p3: In 2025, I completed focused training in microservices and software architecture patterns, and I'm deliberately continuing in that direction.

yumasnap.title: YumaSnap - Event Photo Sharing Platform
yumasnap.desc: Events and wedding venues need a way for guests to share photos instantly, without asking everyone to create an account or install an app. YumaSnap solves that with a QR-based upload flow — guests scan a code at the event and start uploading immediately. I designed the upload pipeline on Supabase and AWS S3, and the real-time layer that syncs every guest's gallery as new photos come in.

YumaIdentity.title: YumaIdentity - IAM Service
YumaIdentity.desc: An independently designed and built Identity and Access Management (IAM) service — authentication, role-based authorization, and multi-tenant access control for my own applications. Structured with Clean Architecture on ASP.NET Core and EF Core, with JWT-based sessions and OAuth 2.0 (PKCE) authorization flows, backed by SQL Server and shipped as a Dockerized backend with its own versioned releases. The API is under active development; the admin UI is still in progress.

yumalog.title: YumaLog - Structured Logging & Observability for .NET
yumalog.desc: Enterprise Windows Services and legacy .NET Framework applications often have no consistent way to centralize logs. YumaLog is a structured logging library I built to solve that — a single logging interface that works across both .NET Framework and modern .NET Core/.NET 5+ services. It buffers log events asynchronously, writes them as structured JSON per application, and is designed to be collected by Grafana Alloy and shipped to Loki for querying in Grafana. Ships as a NuGet package with its own test suite and configurable buffering, retention, and diagnostics for rollout.
